requirements.purpose: Online depot access from fleet components
requirements.notes: KB 443166: unrestricted outbound HTTPS from the IPs and FQDNs of the fleet components. eapi.broadcom.com is named for the OAuth token at /vcf/generateToken; dl.broadcom.com for binaries and metadata; vvs.broadcom.com for vLCM compatibility data; vsanhealth.vmware.com for vSAN health and HCL. requirements.purpose: Temporary VMSP bootstrap VM to vCenter
requirements.notes: KB 448888: bootstrap fails with PUBLIC_VSP_CLUSTER_BOOTSTRAP_FAILED when a firewall drops HTTPS from the temporary bootstrap VM to vCenter. The resolution step also calls this TCP port 443.

requirements.purpose: SDDC Manager health check of the VMSP bootstrap VM
requirements.notes: KB 440449: SDDC Manager polls https://<Bootstrap_VM_IP>:5480/health. Allow TCP 5480 in both directions between SDDC Manager and the VMSP cluster or management network used for that VM. The article describes the failure during an NSX firewall exclusion step; the connectivity requirement it states is this health port.

constraints.text: The license server does not communicate with the Internet. There is no external network requirement for the license server. Connected-mode upload to Broadcom is a VCF Operations path, not a license server path.

License Server Networking says no other component needs a connection to the license server beyond vCenter, VCF Operations, and DNS. The Ports tool also publishes an HCX Manager to License Server flow. Treat that conflict as unresolved: this app shows both sources and does not delete the Ports tool row.

License server 9.1.0.0 and 9.1.0.0100 use internal networks 172.16.0.0/12 and 172.17.0.0/16. Do not deploy the license server on 172.16.0.0/12, and do not point it at a gateway that advertises 172.17.0.0/16. From 9.1.0.0200 those limits no longer apply.

License Server Security says the server communicates through the ports listed on the Ports and Protocols tool and that all other inbound and outbound traffic can be blocked. SSH cannot be enabled. The server uses the time of the ESX host that runs it.
vDefend License Hub pools in the Ports tool are not the VCF license server. The diagram keeps License Server in the management domain and draws License Hub with vDefend.

KB 452400: exclude eapi.broadcom.com, vcf.broadcom.com, and dl.broadcom.com from TLS inspection for VCF Operations 9.1 connection mode. KB 441891 says the same exclusion for eapi.broadcom.com and dl.broadcom.com on the online depot. KB 453215 also requires a registered, syncing license server before depot validation and names dl.broadcom.com, eapi.broadcom.com, vvs.broadcom.com, and vsanhealth.vmware.com.
